basis: Toxic injury of the inner-ear labyrinth; chemical toxicity does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Epilepsy syndromes defined by myoclonic seizures; no common additional organ damage across the group.
Peripheral neuropathy and glomerular nephropathy define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 4/12 patients (~33%).
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and obesity define the syndrome; ocular and gastrointestinal dysfunction are reported in only 5-29%.
Inherited movement disorder causing episodic dystonia; muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Craniosynostosis/scoliosis define it; ID 3/3, hearing loss 2/2, severe visual impairment 1/1. Four-axis cap excludes single-case anemia and anal fistula; estimates are small.
Cauda equina nerve-root injury with established neurogenic bladder dysfunction defines this concept; bowel dysfunction is not established as common.
Hypothalamic brain malformation with epilepsy and possible cognitive decline; precocious puberty occurs in some, without evidence of a >=30% frequency.
Umbrella disorder of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; infection is not shared across its subtypes.
Congenital malalignment of the infundibular ventricular septum, classified as a ventricular septal defect.
Intellectual disability/epilepsy, sparse hair and brachydactyly with skeletal abnormalities define Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome.
Congenital cataracts and ichthyosis are the defining manifestations.
Immune deficiency; bronchiectasis and developmental delay each occur in 3/3. Lymphoma is separately diagnosed; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not prove organ dysfunction.
BBS1 spectrum is chiefly Bardet-Biedl syndrome, with retinal degeneration, obesity and polydactyly; renal functional damage is not established in >=30% of BBS1 cases.
Lassa virus infection umbrella includes predominantly mild or asymptomatic infections; severe visceral damage and hearing loss do not meet the group-wide threshold.
ID/developmental delay 80-99%; hearing impairment, strabismus and cardiac malformations each 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia omitted under the four-axis cap.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect causing bleeding; no intrinsic damage to another organ is established.
Developmental disability and limb/skeletal defects define the syndrome; hair abnormalities and hypoplastic toenails occur in 30-79%.
Congenital atrioventricular septal defect with atrial shunting; respiratory infections and dyspnea do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Acute severe thyrotoxicosis; CNS dysfunction/encephalopathy is a major diagnostic feature. Tachycardia alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Nonsyndromic HGSNAT-related rod-cone retinal degeneration; the gene association alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Fungal infection directly involving and damaging the nail.
Glycogen branching defect with hepatic dysfunction (80-99%); myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy each 30-79%. Neurologic disease varies by subtype; skin findings nonspecific.
Nonpsychotic depressive disorder; a purely psychiatric condition without established organ damage.
